title: Insight Forge Setup
intro: Set up your own Insight Forge in about an hour. Enter each value once. The wizard keeps it and fills it into every later step. Each client gets its own database, its own repo and one login.

variables.label: Business name
variables.help: Same as in your intake record.

variables.label: Your GitHub username
variables.help: The account that will own your copy of the app.
variables.pattern_error: Use letters, numbers and hyphens only.

variables.label: Name for your GitHub repo
variables.help: Pick a new name. Example: acme-insight-forge
variables.pattern_error: Use 3-40 lowercase letters, numbers or hyphens.

variables.label: Supabase project ref
variables.help: 20 letters. Find it in your Supabase project URL or Project Settings.
variables.pattern_error: The ref is exactly 20 lowercase letters.

variables.label: Email for your one login
variables.help: Only one person can log in to each Insight Forge.

variables.label: Email address that sends your alerts
variables.help: Must use a domain you verified in your Resend account.

steps.title: Load your intake answers
steps.instructions: You already filled in the Business Onboarding Intake for your business. Open the Your values box above. Paste your intake record into Import values. Then press Import. This wizard keeps every value and fills it into later steps. If you have no intake record, skip the import and type the name below.
steps.verify_hint: Your values shows the business name.

steps.title: Choose your account names
steps.instructions: Each client gets its own GitHub repo and its own Supabase project. Nothing is shared between clients. Type your GitHub username and pick a name for your new repo.
steps.verify_hint: Your app address in Your values shows https://...github.io/... with your names.

steps.title: Create your empty repo
steps.instructions: In your GitHub account, create a new empty repo named {{repo_name}}. Set it to Private. Do not add a README or other files.
steps.verify_hint: The address opens and says the repo is empty.

steps.title: Copy the app code
steps.instructions: Run these commands on your computer. They copy the Insight Forge code into your repo. The code has an old .env file inside. The commands remove it. They also remove the setup-wizard folder.

copy.label: Terminal commands

steps.checkbox_label: The commands ran with no error
steps.verify_hint: Run: git status. It shows .env as deleted.

steps.title: Set your app path
steps.instructions: The app uses the repo name in its web path. Replace the old name in two files. On a Mac, use sed -i '' instead of sed -i.

copy.label: Terminal commands (run inside the folder)
copy.text:
sed -i 's#/knowledge-loom-prismm/#/{{repo_name}}/#' vite.config.ts
sed -i 's#basename="/knowledge-loom-prismm"#basename="/{{repo_name}}"#' src/App.tsx
grep -rn "knowledge-loom-prismm" vite.config.ts src index.html public

steps.verify_hint: If grep prints a line, replace the old name with {{repo_name}} in that file.

steps.title: Create your Supabase project
steps.instructions: In your own Supabase account, create a new project for {{business_name}}. Choose a strong database password and keep it in your password manager. Do not type it here. When the project opens, copy the project ref from its web address. It is the 20 letters before .supabase.co.
steps.verify_hint: Your values shows your Supabase project URL. It opens a page from Supabase.

steps.title: Turn on database extensions
steps.instructions: In Supabase, open Database, then Extensions. Turn on pg_cron and pg_net. The daily jobs need them. VERIFY: If a later step shows an error about cron or net, come back here first.

steps.title: Build the database
steps.instructions: Run these commands inside your repo folder. Do not run the file supabase/seed_knowledge_loom.sql. That file holds another company's content.

copy.label: Terminal commands

steps.checkbox_label: The push finished with no error
steps.verify_hint: Supabase, Table Editor, shows tables such as profiles, readers and content_schedules.

steps.title: Point the daily jobs at your project
steps.instructions: Open the SQL Editor in your Supabase project. Run this SQL. Replace PASTE_YOUR_ANON_KEY with the anon public key from Project Settings, API. That key stays in your Supabase account only. VERIFY: key names app_url and alert_from_email come from the Prismm build.

copy.label: SQL

steps.checkbox_label: The SQL ran and I replaced the key
steps.verify_hint: Run: select key, value from public.automation_config; The URL row shows your URL. The anon key row is not empty.

steps.title: Deploy the server functions
steps.instructions: Run this command in your repo folder. It uploads all the functions.
steps.verify_hint: Supabase, Edge Functions, lists fire-due-schedules and check-approved-queue.

steps.title: Add your email key
steps.instructions: Create a Resend account and verify the domain of {{from_email}}. Then run the command below. Replace PASTE_YOUR_RESEND_KEY in your own terminal. Never paste it in this wizard. VERIFY: the secret name RESEND_API_KEY comes from the check-approved-queue function.
steps.verify_hint: Run: npx supabase secrets list --project-ref {{supabase_project_ref}} It shows RESEND_API_KEY.

steps.title: Add the build settings in GitHub
steps.instructions: In your repo, open Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions. Add three repository secrets with these exact names. For the publishable key, open Supabase, Project Settings, API Keys. Copy the publishable key into GitHub only.

copy.label: Secret 3: name only
copy.text:
VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY
(paste the key from Supabase inside GitHub)

steps.verify_hint: GitHub shows three secrets with these names.

steps.title: Turn on GitHub Pages
steps.instructions: In your repo, open Settings, Pages. Set Source to GitHub Actions.
steps.verify_hint: The Pages screen says the site is ready to publish.

steps.title: Publish the app
steps.instructions: Run these commands in your repo folder. The push starts the build.

copy.label: Terminal commands
copy.text:
git add -A
git commit -m "Set up Insight Forge for {{business_name}}"
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main

steps.verify_hint: Your repo, Actions tab, shows a green check. Then {{app_url}} opens the login page.

steps.title: Create your one login
steps.instructions: In Supabase, open Authentication, Users, then Add user. Use the email below and set a password in Supabase. Then open Sign In / Providers and turn off Allow new users to sign up. Then open URL Configuration and set Site URL to your app address.
steps.checkbox_label: The user exists and sign up is off
steps.verify_hint: You can log in at {{app_url}} with {{login_email}}.

steps.title: Enter your brand
steps.instructions: Log in. Open Settings and Strategy. Enter your brand values from your intake. Do not import Prismm content. VERIFY: a script that loads the intake record straight into the app is not built yet, so this is manual. Long fields such as description, audience, tone and words to avoid come from your intake record.

copy.label: Brand values

steps.checkbox_label: Brand values are in the app
steps.verify_hint: Settings shows your business name and colors.

steps.title: Add your AI provider
steps.instructions: In the app, open Settings. Choose your AI provider and model. Paste your AI key there. The key stays in your own account and never goes in this wizard.
steps.verify_hint: The app makes a draft with no error.

steps.title: Connect publishing
steps.instructions: VERIFY: Publishing runs through Zernio. In the app, open Settings and use the connect button for LinkedIn or Instagram. Instagram needs a Business or Creator account linked to a Facebook Page.
steps.verify_hint: Settings shows each channel as connected.

steps.title: Run the health check
steps.instructions: Open the health check page. Fix any red item, then reload.
